ci(release): split installers and CLI into parallel jobs

Create a shared draft release first, then build desktop installers
and agentero CLI on separate matrix jobs so one side can fail without
blocking the other, and CLI skips Node/frontend setup.

docs: link ROADMAP issue #41 in github-project

fix(build): silence Windows dead-code/needless-return in paths

The remote-vault merge left two clippy issues that surface on Windows
builds (and would fail a `clippy -D warnings` CI gate):

- home_dir() is only called from #[cfg(not(windows))] branches, so it
  was dead code on Windows. Gate it with #[cfg(not(windows))].
- xdg_config_home/xdg_cache_home used `return` as the tail of a
  #[cfg(windows)] block; on Windows that is a needless return. Use the
  block tail expression instead.

No behavior change; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings
is now clean on Windows.

fix(agent): prefer .exe/.cmd over bare sh script in Windows PATH resolution

npm global install drops a bare shell script alongside .cmd/.ps1 shims.
The fallback loop checked the bare file first (is_executable returns true
for any file on Windows), handing an invalid sh script to CreateProcess and
failing the ACP probe for npm-installed adapters like codex-acp.

fix(viewer): load local PDFs from bytes to fix "not loaded" on Windows

Local PDFs were read into a blob: URL and handed to EmbedPDF, which
fetch()es it. blob: fetching is fragile in the app webview (already
noted for the wasm worker that stalls re-fetching from blob:); on
Windows WebView2 the document fetch fails, surfacing as
"Document ... not loaded".

Feed PDFium the ArrayBuffer directly via DocumentManager's { buffer }
option (localFileToArrayBuffer); remote https PDFs still use { url }.
Threaded through the tab as pdfBytes (transient, not persisted). Also
logs the previously-swallowed local-read errors for diagnosis.

fix(viewer): guard PdfViewerInner with DocumentContent to prevent "not loaded" crash

PdfViewerInner (and its capability hooks / AnnotationRendererProvider)
rendered before EmbedPDF finished loading the document from the buffer,
throwing "Document ... not loaded" caught by the workspace ErrorBoundary.

Wrap PdfViewerInner in <DocumentContent documentId={docId}> so it only
mounts once the document is loaded (showing a loading state meanwhile).
This is the pattern recommended by the EmbedPDF docs.

fix(pdf): prevent white screen from document close/open race on remount

React StrictMode and tab remount dispose the previous EmbedPDF registry,
whose closeDocument (MEDIUM priority) raced behind the new registry's
openDocumentBuffer (CRITICAL priority) on the shared engine. Because the
PDFium cache keyed document handles by id and ignored re-opens, the stale
close disposed the freshly opened document, so every page render failed
with "document does not open" while the page count still displayed.

Patch @embedpdf/engines PdfCache with reference counting: re-opens bump the
count and release the redundant native handles; close only disposes when the
last owner releases the document.

perf(pdf): unmount inactive PDF tabs and memoize page renderer

All open tabs stayed mounted (tabs.map + hidden), so every PDF tab kept its
PDFium document and 11 plugins alive on the shared main-thread engine,
making the app lag badly with many papers open. Only mount the EmbedPDF
viewer for the active tab; reading position, annotations and ask threads
are persisted, so remounting restores them. Also hoist the Scroller
renderPage callback into a memoized useCallback to avoid re-running the
per-page pin/filter work on plain scroll/zoom re-renders.

perf(settings): keep visited panes mounted for instant section switches

Settings sections were conditionally rendered, so every switch unmounted the
current pane and remounted the target one — re-running each pane's load
effects (agent list, connector status, remote-cache stats, dynamic imports)
and causing a visible hitch before the new section appeared. Track visited
sections and keep their panes mounted but hidden, so switches are instant and
data is loaded once per visit. Scroll resets to top on section change.

perf(tabs): cut tab switch lag with PDF LRU mounting and stable TabCenter props

Switching between paper tabs re-opened the PDFium document every time (the
prior change unmounted all inactive PDF tabs), which blocks the main thread
and caused a hitch on each switch. Keep a most-recently-used set of PDF tabs
mounted (active + last few) so switching between recent papers is instant
while older tabs still release their engine document.

Also stabilize the two inline callback props passed to TabCenter
(onLibraryColumnsChange, onOpenSettings) with useCallback so its React.memo
can bail out on unrelated App re-renders — previously every mounted tab's
viewer/editor re-rendered on any App state change.

revert(ci): drop PDFium runtime prep step

Removes the "Prepare PDFium runtime" step so the Rust job runs
`cargo test --workspace` directly, matching the workflow before the
workaround, to verify whether CI still fails without it.

This reverts commit 81d5fdcfc55dbeda1724a23acbe3d0fe5e77bbb2.

ci: Provision PDFium binary for macOS tests

The rust-cache action skips the liteparse-pdfium-sys build script on
cache hits, leaving libpdfium.dylib missing during dlopen. Download
the binary explicitly and export PDFIUM_LIB_PATH/INCLUDE_PATH so both
build and test steps find it.

ci: drop hardcoded pnpm version in release workflow

The pinned "version: 10" conflicted with packageManager "pnpm@11.5.3"
in package.json, causing pnpm/action-setup to fail with
ERR_PNPM_BAD_PM_VERSION. Rely on package.json as the single source of
truth, matching ci.yml.

refactor(tauri): gate desktop-only plugins and commands for iOS

feat(ui): global UI scale with discrete presets and keyboard shortcuts

- Replace the per-button toolbarIconSize setting with a global uiScale
  setting (80% / 90% / 100% / 125% / 150% presets) that scales the
  entire interface via the root html font-size.
- Toolbar buttons and title bar now scale together with the rest of the
  UI; remove the explicit CSS vars in WorkspaceHeader and LayoutMenu.
- Add Cmd/Ctrl +/-/0 shortcuts (zoomIn / zoomOut / zoomReset) that jump
  between presets, matching common editors and browsers.
- Persist uiScale in Rust AppSettings and snap values to the preset
  list in both frontend and backend normalization.
- On macOS, newly created windows position traffic lights according to
  the current uiScale.

docs(ui): document global UI scale presets and zoom shortcuts

- Add UI Scale description to the Appearance conventions.
- Document Cmd/Ctrl +/-/0 zoom shortcuts in the shortcuts table.

fix(ui): keep virtualized lists and core fonts in sync with uiScale

- Add useUiScale() hook so components can react to scale changes without
  re-rendering on every settings change.
- Make file-tree and papers-library virtualizer estimateSize scale-aware
  so row offsets and total height stay correct when the interface is
  zoomed, preventing overlap.
- Convert hard-coded px font sizes in file-tree, papers-library, and
  document-tab-bar to rem equivalents so they scale with the rest of the
  interface.

feat(file-tree): add new file, new folder and copy path to context menu

right-click context menu. Creation uses the clicked folder (or the
parent folder when right-clicking a file) as the destination.

fix(ui): scale ViewModeToggle thumb with root font size

The sliding thumb used hardcoded 24px/2px offsets while the buttons
and gaps are Tailwind rem classes, so the thumb drifted at non-default
uiScale. Use rem values so the thumb stays aligned with the buttons.

fix(viewer): allow switching back to PDF loaded from bytes

modeAvailable only checked pdfUrl, but local PDFs are often loaded as
pdfBytes with a null url. After switching to HTML the PDF button was
disabled and the view could not return to PDF. Check pdfBytes as well.

refactor(viewer): measure ViewModeToggle thumb from active button layout

Replace the hardcoded cell/gap offsets with ResizeObserver + offset
measurements of the active button. The sliding indicator now stays
aligned at any uiScale and adapts automatically if button sizes change.

feat(lookup): batch identifier import with deduplication and concurrency

Add lookup_import_batch Tauri command that parses, deduplicates and imports
multiple identifiers concurrently with a configurable concurrency limit.
Emit count-based progress events under a single background task id.
Support local and remote vaults.

feat(settings): add batchImportConcurrency preference

Expose batch import concurrency (1-10, default 3) in AppSettings,
Rust settings store, and the General settings pane with i18n labels.

i18n(lookup): batch import and queued download strings

Add English and zh-CN translations for batch import summary,
download queue details, and count-based progress display.

feat(lookup): wire up batch magic-wand import and per-paper download queue

Replace the single-line magic-wand input with an auto-growing textarea,
split pasted identifiers on multiple separators, and call
lookup_import_batch. Open the first successful paper and enqueue each
missing-asset paper as its own queued download task via the new
runQueuedBackgroundTask helper.

docs(lookup): document batch import, concurrency setting and test cases

Update API contract, identifier-lookup spec, UI docs and roadmap/todo
with batch separator rules, lookup_import_batch parameters, the new
batchImportConcurrency setting, and manual test cases with expected UI
behavior.

refactor(core): deduplicate background-task lifecycle

fix(host): use a Windows-compatible Claude ACP install command

The Claude ACP install command hard-coded a Unix user-prefix
(`--prefix "$HOME/.local"`). On Windows cmd.exe `$HOME` does not expand
and `~/.local/bin` is not on PATH, so the install landed in the wrong
place and the binary was never found. Use a plain `npm i -g` on Windows
(npm's global prefix is already on PATH) and keep the user-prefix install
on Unix.

fix(host): resolve USERPROFILE when opening the install terminal on Windows

The install terminal was launched with `wt -d %USERPROFILE%`, but Rust's
Command spawns wt without a shell, so %USERPROFILE% was passed literally
and wt resolved it against the app cwd, failing with 0x8007010b ("cannot
access startup directory"). Resolve the real profile path before spawning,
falling back to the temp dir (which always exists at that point).

fix(import): parse PDFs from memory so PAPER.md works with non-ASCII paths on Windows

liteparse was handed the PDF as a filesystem path, which goes through
FPDF_LoadDocument. On Windows that path handling is unreliable for
non-ASCII paths (e.g. a Chinese 文档 segment in a OneDrive vault), so
Zotero-imported papers silently failed to generate PAPER.md. Read the PDF
with std::fs (Unicode-safe) and pass it to liteparse as PdfInput::Bytes
(FPDF_LoadMemDocument), which has no path step. Covers the Zotero migrate,
asset download, and manual parse flows, which all share this helper.

fix(window): use native decorations on Windows/Linux

The frameless windows drew their own caption buttons in React, which
relied on IPC permissions the settings window never had, so on Windows
its close/minimize/maximize controls were dead and a stale singleton
made Settings appear unopenable. Switch all windows to native OS
decorations (macOS keeps its Overlay traffic lights), drop the custom
WindowControls component, and whitelist the settings window in the
capability so keyboard close and cross-window toggle work.
fix(ci): refresh Homebrew release checksums

fix(window): create webview windows from async commands

On Windows the native Settings window opened blank and could not be
closed (release builds included): the logs showed `op start
settings_window_open` with the right URL but no matching `op end`, so
`WebviewWindowBuilder::build()` never returned.

Sync `#[tauri::command]` handlers run on the main thread *inside* the
calling webview's IPC callback. Building another webview from there
hangs: wry waits in a nested message loop for the WebView2 controller
callback, which WebView2 only dispatches once the current event handler
returns. The window shell appeared, its URL never loaded, so no JS ran
and the Esc/⌘W handlers did not exist either.

Make `settings_window_open` and `window_new` async so creation is queued
onto the event loop instead, spawn `window_new` from the macOS menu
handler, and emit `settings_window_closed` when creation fails so the
`⌘,` toggle cannot get stuck in the "open" state.

fix(settings): keep the settings window light and always dismissible

The settings webview shares `main.tsx` with the workspace, so it parsed
the full `App` module graph before rendering its own lightweight root —
noticeable when opening Appearance on Windows. Import `App` dynamically
so only the workspace route pays for it.

Also handle a rejected `boot()`: it used to leave an empty `<body>` with
no key handlers, which looked like a blank window that could not be
dismissed. Render the error and wire Esc / ⌘W to close the window.

fix(ios): re-export IPA with embedded provisioning profile for TestFlight

`tauri ios build --export-method app-store-connect` auto-generates an
ExportOptions.plist with `signingStyle: manual` + `teamID` but no
`provisioningProfiles` mapping. The export step's
IDEDistributionEmbedProfileStep then skips embedding the profile, and
altool rejects the IPA with 90174 ("Missing Provisioning Profile").

The PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER env var only affects the archive
step; the export step reads from ExportOptions.plist. Run `tauri ios
build` to produce the archive, then re-run `xcodebuild -exportArchive`
with a hand-written plist that maps the bundle id to the resolved
profile UUID. Refuse to upload if the resulting IPA still has no
embedded.mobileprovision.

feat(logging): time frontend boot stages

A slow settings window could not be diagnosed from the logs: `boot` only
emitted `op start frontend_boot` with no matching end, so there was no
way to tell whether the delay came from the settings IPC, the theme
table, the language pack or module loading — leaving guesswork.

Log a cumulative `boot stage=<name> ms=<n>` line per step plus the
matching `op end frontend_boot`, tagged `window=main|settings` so the two
webviews can be told apart. Timing is based on `performance.now()`,
measured from navigation start, so the numbers also cover index.html and
the entry module rather than just the await chain.

perf(settings): load only what the settings window needs

Opening Settings stalled for seconds before it accepted scrolling or a
section switch. `visitedSections` only controls mounting, not module
loading, so the statically imported panes pulled the whole settings
surface — including the 1000-line agent pane and its model picker — into
the first paint. main.tsx also imported the PDF engine host and KaTeX
styles eagerly, which the settings webview has no use for.

Split the panes into per-section chunks and let the PDF engine and KaTeX
ride along with `App`. The pane for the *current* section is preloaded
next to the shell instead of being left behind `lazy()`: measured boot is
only ~240ms, so a lazy default pane would just move the stall to right
after the window first looks interactive. Each pane gets its own Suspense
boundary so a section that is still loading cannot blank out the visited
panes kept mounted beside it.

First-paint chunks for the settings window drop from 52.8 kB to 8.3 kB of
shell plus the section's own pane.

chore(deps): patch @embedpdf/plugin-tiling for dpr override and tile placeholders

chore(deps): patch @embedpdf/engines to surface worker init failures

The worker engine's RemoteExecutor ignored worker-side "wasmError"
messages and onerror events, so any worker init failure left the
ready task pending forever and every document operation queued
silently ("loading" forever in Tauri webviews). Reject the ready task
on those failures and expose a whenReady() probe on both engine
factories so the host can verify readiness and fall back.

chore(deps): pin @types/react-dom via workspace override

pnpm patch-commit re-resolves the store and keeps drifting
@types/react-dom to the newest patch release. Pin it with a workspace
override so future patch workflows stop touching unrelated lockfile
entries.

perf(pdf): prefer worker engine with readiness probe and direct fallback

Run PDFium WASM in a Web Worker so zoom/scroll rasterization no longer
blocks the UI thread. The host verifies the worker with a whenReady()
handshake plus an 8s timeout and falls back to the main-thread engine
when the worker cannot boot in a webview, remembering the failure for
the process lifetime. The wasm URL is resolved to an absolute URL
before handoff because blob-URL workers cannot resolve page-relative
paths.

perf(pdf): cap raster devicePixelRatio at 1.5

Full devicePixelRatio rasters on high-DPI screens make every zoom step
and scroll re-render heavy while PDFium rasterizes on the UI thread.
Cap the raster dpr at 1.5 for RenderLayer and TilingLayer (the dpr
prop comes from the plugin-tiling patch); agent region crops keep
their own resolution.

perf(pdf): coalesce ctrl+wheel zoom steps per animation frame

Trackpad pinch fires many wheel events per second and the handler
applied a zoom step per accumulated threshold inside each event,
re-rasterizing every visible page per event. Accumulate deltas across
events and apply the net steps once per animation frame
(createWheelZoomCoalescer), keeping the toolbar-style fixed increments
and the 150ms gesture reset.

perf(pdf): pre-render outer tile ring to reduce scroll pop-in

Tiling defaults to extraRings: 0, so fast scrolling exposes blank page
edges until tiles rasterize. Pre-render one ring of tiles around the
viewport; with the worker engine this extra rendering stays off the
main thread.

perf(pdf): skip marks poll re-render when content unchanged

perf(pdf): enlarge tiling tiles to reduce worker round-trips

The single PDFium worker serializes every render request, so long
documents fast-scrolling through many 768px tiles queue up visibly.

per viewport.

perf(pdf): cap RenderLayer base-coat scale at 1.5

RenderLayer rasterizes the whole page at the current zoom on every
zoom change; on long documents these full-page rasters (and their
worker→main blob transfers) dominate because the single worker
serializes them. The layer is only the base coat under the sharp
TilingLayer, so cap its scale at 1.5: past that zoom whole pages stop
re-rendering entirely while tiles keep the viewport sharp.

fix(zotero): restore full collection tree and exclude addon junk

Second-level collection folders vanished after migration for two
reasons. chosen_collection_path picked the lexicographically smallest
full path, so items belonging to both a parent and a child collection
were absorbed by the parent; and folders only materialized as a side
effect of item placement, so empty or deduped collections never
appeared. Pick the deepest (most specific) path instead and create the
whole collection tree up front when collection folders are enabled.

Also exclude computerProgram items — Zotero add-ons create them (e.g.
literally titled "Addon Item") and they must never become papers — and
surface each item's type in the scan preview.

feat(zotero): relocate existing papers into the collection tree

Re-migrations previously skipped every deduped paper, so vaults
imported before the collection-tree fix stayed flat forever. On a
dedup hit, when the paper sits outside its collection folder, move
the folder into place and rewrite the catalog row (keyed by path).
Refuses to overwrite anything on disk or in the catalog and rolls the
folder back if the catalog rewrite fails. Result exposes a relocated
count.

fix(zotero-sync): use Zotero 7 rich-note format and stop garbage recursion

Diagnosed against the user's real library: pushed notes lacked the
`<div class="zotero-note znv1">` wrapper, so Zotero treated them as
legacy plain-text notes — displaying HTML tags literally, then escaping
the whole content on save (`<p>`), which destroyed the sync
markers. Every later push then created a NEW note (duplicates), and pull
re-imported the escaped notes as "user notes", appending escaped garbage
back into NOTES.md — growing each round and making sync crawl.

Fixes:
- wrap pushed notes in the Zotero 7 rich-note wrapper (renders as HTML,
  markers survive)
- reclaim escaped/damaged notes via the loose `agentero:sync paper=<id>`
  signature (LIKE wildcards escaped); duplicates move to Zotero trash,
  unchanged content is not rewritten
- pull/migration skip anything carrying the signature in any escape form
- pull self-heals NOTES.md first: strips leaked `---`-separated sync
  blocks, preserving frontmatter and user content verbatim

Verified with 22 codec tests in an isolated harness; the user's polluted
vault NOTES.md files were repaired separately with backups.

perf(pdf): coalesce viewport scroll metrics per frame

A trackpad emits scroll events faster than the display refresh, and each
commit pushed a fresh scroller layout through EmbedPDF, re-rendering every
mounted page more than once per frame.

perf(pdf): precompute layout hit regions per page

Each mounted page ran whole-document NMS (and, with the debug Eye on,
spurious-detection suppression) during render, so one scroll re-render cost
about ten redundant O(n^2) passes. Bucket regions by page once per region-set
change and let renderPage do a map lookup.

perf(pdf): keep wheel listener passive while scrolling

The Ctrl/Cmd+wheel zoom handler was permanently non-passive, so every wheel
tick had to reach the main thread before the viewport could scroll. Attach the
non-passive listener only while a zoom gesture is possible and swap to a
passive one for the duration of a plain scroll gesture.
docs(pdf): note scroll-path and wheel passivity optimizations

perf(references): carry citation ordinal through the filter

Each rendered card recovered its number with citations.indexOf(), making the
list O(n^2) in reference count.

perf(pdf): mount fewer off-screen pages

The scroll plugin default buffer keeps about eight off-screen pages mounted,
so every scroller layout change re-rendered ten page subtrees.

perf(pdf): build gutter pins once per mark change

Pin placement walks the page's whole text-rect list, and renderPage rebuilt
all four pin pipelines for every mounted page on every scroll re-render. Pins
are now bucketed by page in one memo, and annotation rects are normalized when
highlights are rebuilt instead of read from the plugin during render.

perf(pdf): memoize per-page overlay layers

Every mounted page re-renders when the scroller layout changes, so the gutter,
citation links and translate overlay all rebuilt their subtrees. Memoize the
three layers and give them stable prop identities (shared empty arrays, hoisted
layer style) so unchanged pages can bail out.

perf(pdf): refresh marks from the vault watcher instead of a timer

Every 4s tick re-read all mark files over serial IPC and JSON-fingerprinted
them just to find nothing changed. Marks now refresh on vault:file-changed
events under the paper's marks/ folder, coalesced over 200ms, keeping the
become-active and window-focus catch-ups.

refactor(pdf): extract EmbedPDF annotation highlights into use-pdf-highlights

Highlights are real PDF annotations owned by the EmbedPDF annotation plugin,
so their whole lifecycle (import/migrate on open, event subscription, debounced
export to marks/annotations.json) is one boundary that nothing else in the
viewer needs to see. `PdfViewerInner` only consumed the resulting arrays.

Move that cluster into a hook: the highlight/anchor/citation-link states with
their single writer `rebuildHighlights`, the debounced save, both effects, and
the annotation write primitives (create / comment / delete). The note editor
keeps its own state in the parent because opening it reads the card cluster;
it now delegates the annotation writes to the hook.

sets, same published view models.

refactor(pdf): extract persisted mark IO into use-pdf-marks-io

Ask threads, translate records and visual agent-trace marks share one IO
lifecycle: a single `list*` fan-out on open, one Vault-watcher subscription with
its 200 ms burst coalescing and fingerprint guard, the become-active / focus
catch-ups, and one publish path to the annotations panel. That machinery was
interleaved with the ask and translate workflows in `PdfViewerInner`, so the
reason a refresh must never commit an unchanged array (page twitching) was far
from the code that guards it.

Move the three arrays, their mirror refs and the pure `upsert*` state updaters
into one hook. Everything that writes a mark to disk stays with its workflow and
now uses the returned setters, which are stable identities added to the existing
dependency lists so the effect and callback semantics are unchanged.

refactor(pdf): extract text-selection detection into use-pdf-text-selection

Selection detection and the copy interception were two effects sitting far apart
in `PdfViewerInner`, between unrelated clusters, even though they are one
concern: an EmbedPDF drag selection becomes a placed action menu, is published
to the Agent selection store, and — because a PDFium selection is invisible to
the DOM — must hijack ⌘/Ctrl+C while that menu is open.

Move detection, menu placement and menu state into a hook. The menu's actions
stay with their owning clusters (highlight, note, ask, add-to-chat, translate)
and keep being passed into the card stack by the parent, so this is a boundary
around "where is the menu", not "what does it do".

The hook is called after hostRef/zoomRef because it needs both injected. Call
sites that only clear the menu now list the returned stable setter, leaving the
dependency sets semantically unchanged.

refactor(pdf): extract selection translate into use-pdf-selection-translate

The 翻译 workflow was ~200 lines inside PdfViewerInner: the ephemeral card's
streaming state, its cancel token, two provider paths (ACP Agent listeners vs
plain translate provider), the record write to marks/<id>.json and the failure
chrome. None of it is read outside the translate card, so it belongs in one hook
with an explicit boundary instead of the shared closure.

usePdfCards must stay declared first (translate opens and hides cards), so the
two cards→translate edges — cancelling a run on card switch and clearing the
error chrome on open/close — go through refs assigned right after the hook, and
the translateStreaming mirror ref is created in the parent and injected. The
agent session token stays in the parent because the ask cluster shares it.

No behavior change: same streaming semantics, persistence points, i18n keys and
notifyError strings.

with the formula glossary card, so both states keep one owner (the layout
cluster, extracted next). To make that possible without splitting the invariant,

fix(pdf): extend document ref-count patch to the worker-engine cache

The 0.5.3 regression "layout analysis failed: document does not open"
followed by blank PDF pages is the same close/open race fixed earlier
(be8ecade): on tab remount the stale registry's closeDocument (MEDIUM
priority) races behind the new registry's openDocumentBuffer (CRITICAL)
on the shared engine, and the stale close disposes the freshly opened
document so every render fails.

That fix only patched the direct-engine PdfCache. The worker engine's
inlined worker-side PdfCache (the engine actually in use) never got the
reference counting, so re-opens were ignored and one close disposed a
still-referenced document. Extend the pnpm patch with identical
ref-counting for the worker-side cache: re-opens bump the count and
release the redundant native handles; close only disposes when the last
owner releases. Verified the decoded worker source parses cleanly.

fix(pdf): harden the click-to-annotate hit target

Moving activation from hover dwell to click left the affordance missing
the guarantees a click needs:

- Browsers dispatch `click` whenever pointerdown and pointerup share an
  element, so a text-selection drag or pan starting inside a figure
  opened a crop card. Restore a 6px travel tolerance; keyboard
  activation (`detail === 0`) bypasses it since it has no travel.
- Hover only tinted the region 5%, so the bbox that the click crops was
  not visible before committing. Frame it on hover, and on
  `focus-visible` too — a translucent UA ring over arbitrary page
  content is not a reliable keyboard landmark.
- The hint chip is a fixed-size label inside a zoom-scaled box, so on
  small regions it spilled over neighbouring content. Gate it on a
  minimum region size and clamp it.
- PDFium renders the crop asynchronously with nothing on screen in
  between, so a click read as a no-op. Frame the in-flight region and
  spin.
- The label enumerated "figure, table, or algorithm" although
  `region.kind` is known, and said 标注 where the product says 批注.

Formula-legend regions have no click action, so they get onFocus/onBlur
to stay reachable without a pointer, and a help cursor; annotate regions
use a crosshair, leaving the pointer cursor to citation links.

fix(jobs): 让 JobCenter runner 真正执行

`try_start` 已把 job 置为 `Running` 并占用 kind 并发额度，而每个
`run_*_job` 首行又调 `mark_running`——它只接受 `Queued`，于是必定返回
None、runner 立刻 return。全部 6 个 spawn 点都先调 `try_start`，因此
ParseBody / ParseRefs / LayoutAnalyze / DownloadAssets 从来没有真正跑过：
job 永久停在 `Running`，`running_by_kind` 不回落，cap=1 的 kind 第一个
job 就把车道焊死，任务面板只剩一行 0% 的排队。

改为由 `try_start` 把 `StartedJob` 交给 runner，runner 不再自行转换状态；
新增 `spawn_runner` 收敛 6 处重复的 dispatch。类型上也不再可能凭 job id
启动一个未经 `try_start` 的 runner。

`JobSnapshot` 顺带暴露 `force`，供渲染进程重建 offer 时使用。

fix(jobs): 修复渲染进程 offer 链路

`job:offer` 的 payload 是平铺的，而 listener 按 `job:changed` 的
`{job}` 形状读 `event.payload.job`，取到 undefined，于是没有任何
executor 匹配得上：LayoutAnalyze job 白等 15 分钟超时，期间 cap=1 的
车道一直被占。

同时补掉这条链路上其余会挂住任务或跑偏的地方：

- offer 走统一 dispatch：按 jobId 去重，executor 抛错兜底上报
  `failed`，让 Rust 立刻释放并发额度而不是等超时。
- offer 是 fire-and-forget，listener 挂上后 `job_list` 一次，重新认领
  Rust 已置 `running` 的可执行 kind（重载 / 首帧竞态丢的那一份）。
- headless 分析接受调用方给的 documentId，进度按它过滤，不再把 viewer
  内另一次分析的百分比报到这个 job 上；收尾清掉一次性的 store 条目。
- 取消真正 abort layout task，不再只是 reject 掉 promise、让 ONNX 跑完
  并写出被取消 job 的 sidecar。
- `jobReport` 全部带 catch：上报失败不再逃逸成未处理拒绝。
- `cancelled` 的面板行改走 `cancelBackgroundTask`，会被 prune 掉。

fix(catalog): 外部改动 PDF/TeX/PAPER.md 后失效 CapsCache

`PaperCaps` 按论文缓存一整个会话，只有 Host 自己的写路径会
`invalidate`。外部编辑器、CLI、Agent 子进程或用户手删 PAPER.md 之后，
缓存继续按旧快照回答，`job_reconcile_paper` 的 `needs_paper_md()` 因此
判假，打开论文时一个任务都不排——PAPER.md 永远补不出来（同一次打开里
ParseBody 缺席而 ParseRefs 正常，因为后者直接看磁盘上的 sidecar）。

Vault watcher 已经知道哪些路径变了，就在那里失效对应论文的缓存：只对
决定 caps 的文件（PDF / .tex / .ltx / PAPER.md）动作，并同时失效父级与
上一级目录，因为 PDF/TeX 可能落在 `source/` 里。

fix(zotero-import): honor selected folder for multi-collection items, report duplicates

Diagnosed against the user's real library: 8 duplicate item pairs exist
(the same paper saved twice in Zotero, in different sub-collections).
Two confusions followed:

- Placement ignored the folder being imported: an item belonging to
  several collections always landed at its globally deepest path, so
  importing folder A could put the paper under folder B instead.
- Dedup (arXiv/DOI/title) silently skipped the second copy of a
  duplicate pair, making it look like the paper was never imported.

Fixes:
- migrate accepts preferCollection (the dialog passes its folder
  filter); placement then prefers the item's own collection inside the
  selected subtree over a deeper unrelated branch.
- duplicate items merged into an existing paper are counted
  (mergedDuplicates) and shown in the migration summary, so skips are
  explained instead of silent. Notes/annotations of duplicates keep
  backfilling into the surviving paper as before.

fix(pdf-translate): batch layout paragraphs for contextual full-text translation

Full-text (layout) translation sent every detected paragraph as an isolated
request, so engines had no surrounding context and output was inconsistent.
Group paragraphs into reading-order batches (payload <= 4500 chars, ~one
double-column page) joined with [[n]] markers, translate each batch in a single
request, then split the result back by marker and write it to each region's
original bbox. On a marker-parse mismatch the batch falls back to per-paragraph
translation, so no block is lost. Positions/sidecar cache are unchanged since
results are still keyed per region id.

Also nudge the Agent and OpenAI-compatible prompts to preserve the [[n]]
markers and paragraph count when present.

See also: https://github.com/markrahq/markra/pull/368

perf(host): run heavy IO commands off the main thread

Sync #[tauri::command] handlers execute on the main thread, which on
Windows is also the UI message pump, so every heavy-IO sync command
(vault tree walk, full-text search, wiki rebuild, catalog SQLite,
doctor repairs, Zotero scan/sync, font scan, staged imports, refs
graph) froze the whole window while it ran.

- add core::blocking::run_blocking (tauri spawn_blocking wrapper) and
  convert all heavy-IO commands in vault/search/wiki/catalog/usage/
  doctor/zotero_sync/import/refs/settings/export to async fn with the
  blocking body on the blocking pool; JSON contract unchanged
- hold WikiIndex and ExternalRenameRepairStore behind Arc so the
  lock+work closure can move into spawn_blocking (semantics unchanged)
- connector: set_enabled/set_port/start_server become truly async and
  await the TcpListener bind instead of block_on
- list_system_fonts: cache the font list per process (OnceLock)
- tests: run_blocking off-thread assertions + a 300-file vault_search
  benchmark proving the command path runs on the blocking pool

perf(vault): reuse caps cache for tree source probing

vault_tree_build/vault_tree_children re-walked every paper's source/
(often hundreds of arXiv e-print files) on each build to compute the
source shell's hasTex, which dominates tree build time on NTFS. Route
the probe through the managed CapsCache keyed by paper folder, and
widen watcher caps invalidation to all ancestor dirs so deep source
writes still refresh the paper's cached entry. Warm rebuilds of a
20-paper/200-file vault drop from ~12.8ms to ~0.7ms in the new
timing test.

perf(catalog): reuse persistent sqlite connections per vault

Every catalog API paid Connection::open + 4 PRAGMAs + a full migrate()
walk per call, which is expensive on Windows/NTFS. Cache one
Mutex-guarded connection per canonicalized vault root (with_catalog),
opening and migrating only on first use, and drop stale handles when
catalog.sqlite disappears so vault deletion/recreation recovers.
Also memoize per-path is_dir stats in dedupe_records_by_id. 200x
paper_list drops from ~126ms (fresh opens) to ~24ms with exactly one
physical open in the new timing test.

perf(wiki): incremental index rebuild with lookup resolve and row-level cache

Watcher/rename-triggered wiki rebuilds re-resolved every occurrence with a
linear document scan (O(E×D)), re-read the whole sqlite snapshot, and rewrote
every row on any change — the dominant Windows stall around Vault edits.

- resolve: prebuilt DocumentLookup maps (exact/lowercase path, segment
  suffix, stem, alias) drop resolution to ~O(E); priority semantics are
  byte-for-byte identical, proven by a reference-scan equivalence test.
- index: rebuilds keep stat fingerprints in memory; unchanged fingerprints
  return immediately, partial changes reuse in-memory parse products and only
  re-read changed files. Rename transactions' pre/post rebuilds become cheap
  freshness checks.
- cache (schema v3): stores per-file parse products only (documents +
  occurrences keyed by source), verified by row-level hashes instead of a
  whole-snapshot JSON SHA-256; persist upserts/deletes just the changed rows,
  and load re-resolves against the full document set so cross-file resolution
  changes never go stale.

Release benchmark (1000 files x 5 links, macOS): cold rebuild 1343ms -> 56ms,
one-file-changed rebuild 1339ms -> 15ms, no-change rebuild 13.5ms -> 3.8ms,
rename transaction 1346ms -> 20ms.

perf(library): batch reading activity IPC and keep heatmap cache warm

Switching back to the Library used to clear the whole heatmap cache and
re-read marks per paper (3+ IPC each, ~1500-2000 invokes at 500 papers),
a major Windows WebView2 stall. Add paper_reading_activity_batch to read
all marks/*.json sidecars in one IPC (Rust-side parse mirrors the
highlight/ask/translate schemas), refresh activity with 2 IPC total on
activation, and discover missing PDF page counts lazily for visible rows
only (persisted to pdf_page_counts) instead of reopening PDFs in bulk.

perf(agent): coalesce streaming chunks, cap tool payloads, memoize transcript rows

Tame the agent:stream/agent:tool event storm that stalls the webview on
Windows during streaming turns:

- Host coalesces consecutive same-kind text chunks in a ~40ms window
  before emitting agent:stream (kind switches, tool/plan updates and
  completed/failed flush first, so ordering and text stay lossless).
  Unit test: 200 chunks at 10ms cadence now emit 40 events instead of 200.
- agent:tool raw_input/raw_output are capped at 32KB (head + truncated
  marker); the transcript only renders a preview of these payloads.
- ChatTranscript renders each line via a memoized row with an
  identity-stable handler bundle, so streaming updates re-render only the
  active row; updateSessionLines already keeps untouched line refs stable
  (covered by new store tests).

perf(import): throttle download progress events

reqwest yields 8-16KB chunks, so a 20MB PDF emitted 1000-2500
background-task:progress events (x5 with batch import concurrency),
flooding the webview event loop. Emit byte progress only when the
percentage moves >=1 point or >=100ms elapsed since the last emit, and
always emit the final value on completion. Unit test: 2000 chunk
callbacks now produce 102 events (incl. the final one).

perf(editor): debounce word count and fix CJK regex statefulness

The status bar recomputed the full-document word/char count inside the
useEditorSelector selector on every editor change, walking every leaf per
keystroke (~12ms for a 5000-paragraph note). The selector now only returns
the cheap editor.children reference as a change signal and a 400ms debounced
effect performs the full-text stats, so per-keystroke cost drops to one
timer schedule/clear.

Also fix countWords: the CJK regex carried the g flag into .test(), whose
sticky lastIndex misclassified every other identical CJK token as a latin
word run ("汉 汉" counted 3 instead of 2). Use a stateless copy for .test()
and add regression + perf smoke tests.

perf(editor): reload external disk changes in place instead of remounting

applyDiskChange bumped seedKey/notesKey, which keyed the whole MarkdownEditor
and forced a full remount per external write: every plugin re-initialized, the
whole document re-deserialized, scroll and caret lost. An Agent streaming into
an open NOTES.md hit this repeatedly.

The dock view now keys the editor per tab only and passes seedKey/notesKey as
a `reloadKey` prop. On bump, the mounted editor replaces its value in place
via editor.tf.setValue (deserialized seed), preserving the scroll position.
The persistence hook cancels pending autosave, suppresses the resulting value
change (no dirty flag, no autosave), refreshes frontmatter/asset ref-counts,
and a reload generation counter keeps an in-flight persist from settling
stale savedRef/dirty state over the fresh snapshot.

Dirty-tab conflict behavior is unchanged: external content still applies only
after the user confirms the reload toast.

perf(editor): skip full-document serialization for wikilink projection sync

Every wikilink source/display swap (caret crossing a link with arrow keys)
paid two whole-document Markdown serializations: one snapshot before the
projection transform and one comparison in the editor's value-change handler
to decide whether the batch was a user edit.

Projection transforms are Markdown-invariant by construction — the serializer
emits wikiLinkNodeSource(node) || wikiLinkToMarkdown(node), so expanding a
source child, committing parsed attributes or reifying a draft never changes
the serialized document. Track presentation-only batches with a boolean flag
instead: projection sites set it, the explicit real edits that can share a
batch (boundary insertText/insertBreak/delete) clear it, and the value-change
handler consumes it. Serialize count per projection swap drops from 2 to 0.

Behavior is unchanged: presentation-only batches still never mark the
document dirty nor trigger autosave. New vitest coverage proves the
Markdown-invariance the flag relies on.

perf(pdf): parse citation destinations off the main thread with caching

Opening a paper PDF used to re-read the whole file from disk and run
pdf-lib's full object-tree parse (no lazy loading) on the main thread just
to extract hyperref `cite.*` named destinations, blocking scroll/selection
for seconds on 100MB+ papers.

- Parse in a dedicated entity-file module worker (blob-URL workers can
  fail on WebView2); the buffer is transferred, only the small
  coord -> bibtexKey map crosses back.
- Reuse the viewer's already-loaded `tab.pdfBytes` (EmbedPDF structured-
  clones them to its engine worker, so they stay intact): one memcpy
  instead of a second full disk read; disk read remains the fallback.
- Memoize results per `pdfPath:byteLength` so reopening the same PDF never
  parses twice in a session; failures are evicted for retry.
- Defer the build to main-thread idle so it never competes with the
  open-PDF critical path; hover previews resolve once the map is ready.
- logger.debug timing: build source (viewer-bytes/disk), entries,
  duration_ms, cache hits.

fix(file-tree): clear overlay scrollbar and fix tooltip behavior (#347)

## 问题描述

左侧边栏论文列表中，overlay 滚动条（Linux WebKitGTK / macOS WKWebView）
浮在内容上方，8px 宽的点击热区盖住了行末的「精读论文」按钮右半边，
导致点击右半边时触发的是滚动条而非按钮。

同时，各按钮的 Tooltip 存在两个问题：
- 鼠标移出触发按钮后提示框不消失（会因鼠标移到提示框上而保持开启）
- 提示框内文字可被选中，快速移动鼠标时光标变成竖线选择状态

## 根因分析

WebKitGTK 和 WKWebView 使用 overlay 滚动条，不占据布局空间，而是浮在
内容之上并带有 8px 宽的交互热区。Windows WebView2 使用经典占位式滚动
条，本来就占据布局空间，不受此问题影响。

Radix Tooltip 默认开启 hoverable content，鼠标移到提示框上时不会关闭。
提示框内容默认可选中。

## 修复方案

1. FileTreeActions 加 8px 右内边距（pr-2），仅在非 Windows 平台生效
   （getPlatformOS() !== 'windows'），让按钮避开 overlay 滚动条热区
2. 所有 Tooltip 加 disableHoverableContent，鼠标移出触发按钮即消失
3. 所有 TooltipContent 加 select-none cursor-default，禁止文字选中

涉及的四个 Tooltip：展开/折叠附件、下载论文资源、精读论文、下载全部
缺失资源。

feat(lifecycle): support cleanup-returning scoped handlers

The bus only implemented registration, never teardown: handlers could not
return a cleanup, so there was nowhere to express what a vault switch should
release. Split events into scoped (a lifetime, `vault:opened`) and one-shot
facts, and add `emitScoped`, which returns the scope release synchronously so
a React effect can hand it straight to its cleanup — covering switch, close
and unmount without a separate `vault:closed` event.

Scope setup/teardown is serialized per event because setup is async: a fast
switch would otherwise race the old scope's teardown against the new scope's
setup. A scope released before its setup gets a turn skips setup entirely,
which is the StrictMode mount/unmount case.

Registrations are now records rather than raw handler references, fixing
`off()` removing the wrong entry when the same function is registered twice.

feat(core): add listenSafe and migrate leaky event subscriptions

Subscriptions were written as `let off; void (async () => { off = await
listen(...) })(); return () => off?.()`. Because listen() needs a Host
round-trip, disposing before it resolves left `off` undefined, so the cleanup
no-opped and the listener stayed registered forever. StrictMode mounts, then
unmounts, then mounts again on every dev mount, so this fired constantly and
produced duplicate handlers.

listenSafe chains the disposer off the pending promise instead, which is
correct whenever it is called; toSafeDisposer does the same for any other
promise-returning subscribe (bridge and workspace-broadcast helpers).
useTauriEvent covers components whose effect exists purely to subscribe, and
holds the handler in a ref so inline closures no longer resubscribe — the
native menu hook was re-subscribing on all eight of its handler identities.

fix(pdf-translate): clean source text and merge split paragraphs before translating

The PDF text layer reaches the engine with line-break hyphenation, ligatures
and running header/footer runs spliced into the prose, and a paragraph
continued in the next column or page is sent as two half-sentences, so the
output reads broken. Normalize the source, chain continuation fragments into
one request and split the result back per bbox, mask inline math/URL/DOI
tokens, and give both prompt paths academic-translation rules.

Fix #340

fix(bootstrap): correct startup lifecycle ordering and teardown

Four related defects in how the app starts up:

- Store seeding ran inside `useState(() => ...)`, i.e. side effects during
  render, which StrictMode can invoke twice. It moves to `boot()`, which is
  module-level and awaited before createRoot, so the pre-paint guarantee holds
  while the impure render goes away. Same anti-pattern removed from the doc and
  feature window roots.
- The JobCenter effect registered two global subscriptions and returned no
  cleanup, and both starters set their idempotency guard only after `await
  listen(...)` so two synchronous calls each registered a listener.
  `stopJobCenterExecutorListener` existed but was never called. Guards are now
  synchronous and both starters return disposers.
- `app:ready` was emitted while `validateRestoredVault()` was still in flight,
  though its comment claimed the vault was already validated. Validation now
  returns a promise and the event waits for it.
- `window:closed` had two independent raw listeners. It is bridged into the bus
  and handled in the central registry instead, which also drops one leg of the
  pre-existing feature-window/ui-store import cycle.

feat(vault): add vault-scoped store clears

Switching vaults left the previous vault's state behind: catalog rows, wiki
rename flow, agent chat sessions, tab annotations and layout analyses all
survived because these stores have init but no reset. No callers yet — the
vault:opened scope teardown wires them up next.

Each clear is deliberately scoped rather than a full store reset:

- Monotonic signals (trashReloadSignal, wikiIndexRevision, lookupOpenSignal)
  are preserved; zeroing them can match a subscriber's last-seen value and
  swallow an update.
- The agent turn-bridge handler slot is preserved. AgentPanel registers it on
  mount and the panel does not remount on a vault switch, so clearing it would
  break PDF-pin turns until it happened to remount.
- UI chrome and live window truth (rail state, agentPanelMounted,
  featurePoppedOut, settingsOpen) are preserved.
- The library and wiki clears also cancel their pending debounced timers, which
  otherwise outlive the vault they were scheduled for.

feat(lifecycle): release the vault scope on switch

The vault:opened handler now returns a teardown, so what a vault switch sets up
and what it releases live in one place instead of being split between this
registry and activateVault — the gap that let five stores accumulate the
previous vault's state indefinitely. The closure captured vaultId at setup, so
it already names the vault being closed; no previousVaultId field is needed.

Adds a vault_release command to drop the Host catalog connection. That cache is
process-wide and keyed by vault root, and its only eviction path was
with_catalog noticing the database file had vanished, so every vault visited in
a session kept an open SQLite handle and its WAL alive until exit. Skipped for
remote handles, which have no local catalog root.

activateVault keeps its synchronous clears: those stop the first painted frame
of the new vault from showing the old one, which is a different concern from
releasing resources.

fix(host): stop the bridge relay on exit

BridgeController::stop() existed but was never called, so the mobile relay
socket and its spawned control loop only died with the process and paired
clients saw a TCP reset instead of a clean close.

fix(vault): guard wiki rebuild against remote vaults on refresh paths

refreshAll and handleTrashChanged rebuilt the wiki index unconditionally, unlike
trashPathsAndNotify. A remote handle is not a filesystem path, so the rebuild
always fails there and rebuildWikiAndNotify swallows the error — the work was
simply wasted on every manual refresh and recycle-bin restore.

docs(lifecycle): record scoped events, teardown and the listenSafe rule

lifecycle-events.md was still a draft describing an unbuilt design. It now
documents what shipped: the scoped-vs-fact split, why the emitter owns the
scope instead of the bus inferring teardown from a repeat emit (the null-vault,
failed-restore and StrictMode cases that breaks), reverse teardown order, and
per-event serialization.

Also records two decisions so they are not relitigated: vault:closed is
unnecessary because the scope teardown covers it, and app:will-quit is deferred
because an event from RunEvent::Exit cannot flush a debounced write — the
webview is already gone, so that needs CloseRequested plus an ack instead.
Notes why paper:moved / paper:deleted were dropped: the varying refresh tails
are intentional, keyed on whether syncMovedPaths already updated links.

Adds the vault_release command, the catalog connection-cache lifetime, the
vault close/switch flow, an architecture-level lifecycle section, and the
listenSafe / disposer conventions in the shell doc.

feat(refs): discover new papers citing the library

Local TeX/.bbl only knows which papers a paper cites, never the reverse,
so "who cites my library" has to come from an online source. OpenAlex is
unusable for this: its graph barely contains arXiv preprint-to-preprint
edges, so a vault of current preprints scans to almost nothing. Semantic
Scholar has the data but its citations endpoint has no date filter, no
sort and a hard offset cap, so the scan pulls one batch request for the
whole library then fans out per seed with 8-way concurrency.

Raw citers are overwhelmingly noise, dominated by the citers of a few
field-defining classics, so candidates pass three filters: skip
mega-cited seeds, weight overlap by citation IDF, then gate on centered
SPECTER2 max-similarity against the library with a threshold calibrated
from the library itself. Ranking ends in a fixed budget with MMR rather
than tiered thresholds, which keeps the list short without per-folder
tuning.

feat(pdf-locate): resolve a quote to page rects with the PDFium text engine

Marks written outside the viewer had no way to get geometry, so the CLI could
only anchor to layout regions. `features/pdf_locate` searches page text through
the same PDFium build the viewer selects with, returning per-line rects
normalized the way `coords.ts` does, plus the annotations.json reader/writer the
CLI needs to publish highlights.

Matching runs two passes: strict folds whitespace and typographic variants
(curly quotes, dashes, f-ligatures) so a quote copied from TeX matches typeset
text; loose additionally drops hyphens, spaces and undecodable code points,
which is what bridges line-broken hyphenation and fonts with a broken
ToUnicode map (arXiv 2608.02438 returns U+FFFE for a hyphen).

Locating reuses the isolated PDFium worker with a 30s ceiling — an
Agent-facing command must not hang on a broken PDF.

feat(cli): write highlights, 批注 and translations from a text quote

`mark add` required `--region`, so an Agent could annotate figures but not
sentences. It now takes `--quote`, resolves it through the PDF text engine and
publishes highlights into `marks/annotations.json` — the same store the viewer
treats as the source of truth for highlights, so a CLI highlight is
indistinguishable from a hand-drawn one and carries `--comment` as its 批注.
`--page`, `--match-index` and `--all` disambiguate repeated quotes; a quote that
matches nothing fails with `mark_locate_failed` and writes nothing rather than
leaving a mark the reader cannot render.

Also adds `mark update` for comment/color edits, a top-level `translate` command
and `--kind translate` marks over free MT only: the CLI config is isolated from
GUI settings, so commercial keys are unavailable here by design.

Region highlights move to the same annotations store, and ids now come from
`uuid` — the previous clock-seeded generator only mixed low bits upward, so the
k-th id of any process repeated across runs and two marks in one paper collided.

fix(pdf-viewer): pick up marks written while the paper is open

annotations.json was imported once per mount, so a highlight appended by the
CLI stayed invisible in an open reader and the next debounced export dropped it
again. The viewer now watches that file and imports the annotation ids it does
not already track, skipping its own write echoes and deferring while the initial
import is still in flight.

The marks refresh also re-read ask threads and visual traces but not translate
records, so CLI translate marks only appeared after reopening the paper.

fix(network): fall back to the Windows system proxy for Host requests

Users behind Clash/V2RayN-style "system proxy" modes saw pages fail
inside the app (plaza site proxies, feeds, lookups) while their browser

off (the default) every Host request went direct, bypassing the system
proxy that WebView2 and browsers use.

- core/http: detect the Windows system proxy from the registry
  (Internet Settings ProxyEnable/ProxyServer, incl. http=/https=/socks=
  forms) and use it as a fallback whenever the app proxy is off; 30s
  TTL cache follows proxy-software toggles, shared client rebuilds when
  the effective proxy changes.
- network_system_proxy command exposes the detection: the updater
  plugin (own reqwest client) uses it as its proxy fallback, and the
  General settings pane shows "system proxy detected" while the switch
  is off.

fix(network): silence dead_code for proxy parsers on non-Windows CI

parse_windows_proxy_server / with_proxy_scheme are only called from the
Windows branch of system_proxy_url (plus unit tests), so on the macOS CI
runner the lib target saw them as dead code and -D warnings failed the
Rust quality job. Keep them compiled (and unit-tested) on every platform
via cfg_attr allow(dead_code) outside windows+test.
fix(network): match proxy scheme to Windows ProxyServer entry kind

fix(network): correct proxy-parse test expectation for https= entries

The parses_windows_proxy_server_forms test asserted that an `https=`
ProxyServer entry yields an https:// proxy URL, but the parser rightly
returns http://: the http=/https= keys name which traffic a proxy
serves, not how the proxy is reached — the proxy is contacted over plain
HTTP (HTTPS targets tunnel via CONNECT), and an https:// proxy URL would
make reqwest TLS-handshake with a plain HTTP proxy and fail. Fix the
assertion and document the subtlety at the call site.

fix(cli): stop shipping and probing the non-PE Windows CLI stub

End users on a fresh Windows install hit the system dialog "Unsupported
16-bit application ... \??\D:\Agentero\agentero-cli.exe". Root cause: the
desktop bundle shipped the externalBin placeholder — a batch script
renamed to `.exe` — which is not a valid PE image. Double-clicking it, or
the app's CLI discovery probing it with `--version`, made Windows raise
the 16-bit incompatibility dialog. Dev machines never reproduced it
because a real dev CLI resolves before the stub is probed.

Two-layer fix:

- Never execute non-PE files on Windows: `is_plausible_cli_file` now
  requires the MZ magic before any `--version` probe, so batch/shell text
  disguised as `.exe` is skipped silently (plus regression tests).
- Stop shipping the fake executable entirely: drop `externalBin` from
  tauri.conf.json (and the now-dead `cli:bundle:stub` / `cli:ensure`
  scripts, beforeDev/BuildCommand wiring, and release-workflow stub
  steps). Installers no longer contain any agentero-cli file; users get
  the same-version CLI from Settings → About via Release download.

WebView2 WebResourceRequested filters are registered as http://<scheme>.localhost

was never intercepted and failed with ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED when switching to the

fix(import): dedupe magic-wand and PDF imports by shared identifiers

A local PDF whose recognized DOI/arXiv/PMID/ISBN matches an existing

PMID imports without downloadable fulltext), otherwise it goes to

fix(agent): drop synthetic "No response requested." replay placeholders

Claude Code splices synthetic assistant messages (e.g. "No response
requested.") into transcripts when a turn ends without a reply, and
claude-agent-acp replays them verbatim on session/load, so reopened
sessions showed the placeholder as the agent's answer (Fix #411).

turns disappear and mixed turns keep their real parts.

fix(editor): tighten markdown TOC rail and hide its scrollbar

The collapsed rail showed a hover scrollbar and clipped every depth

style(editor): step heading top margins in fixed rem

H1-H3 use mt-6 and H4-H6 mt-4 instead of em-of-heading-size margins, so
section gaps no longer scale with the heading font (H2 sat at ~34px and

fix(editor): break out below horizontal rule on Enter

Void blocks swallow Enter: the caret insertBreak was a no-op and the
block-selection shadow input only re-focused the hr. Insert a paragraph
below the hr for both caret and block-selected Enter, clearing the block

Cover the fixed rem heading scale and the hr Enter break-out in

feat(layout): add MinerU language and force-OCR options

Send the MinerU API `language` (top-level) and per-file `is_ocr` flags
from a collapsible "Advanced" section in the provider card. Options are

Force OCR defaults to off so MinerU keeps deciding per page based on

feat(settings): make auto-opening paper notes optional

Add a General settings toggle `autoOpenPaperNotes` (default on). When
off, opening a paper opens only the PDF/HTML body; NOTES is still one
`⌘\` / "Open notes" away, and the file-tree "Open notes" action forces

Fix #409

perf(editor): stop measuring block margins on every hover

Block drag handles read `getComputedStyle().marginTop` from each block's
`mouseenter`, which also fires for every block scrolling past a resting
pointer and when typing reflows the document — turning a forced style
recalc into per-block editing cost. Top margins are fixed rem keyed by
element type plus the document-start heading reset, so cache on that key.

Also defer the handle menu's `useTranslation`/`t()`/shortcut formatting to
`PopoverContent`'s children, which Radix mounts only once the menu opens.

style(workspace): divide the dockview tab bar from content below

Refs #408

perf(editor): scan only the edited block for TOC headings

`queryTocHeadings` walked the whole document — every element and every text
leaf — and its only cache key was `editor.children` identity, which changes on
every edit. Long notes are exactly the ones that mount the sidebar (it gates on
heading count), so they paid a full traversal per keystroke: measured 0.788ms
on a 600-block / 3441-node document, down to 0.063ms once each subtree's
headings are memoized on the node object. Slate reuses the nodes an edit did
not touch, so a keystroke now re-scans just the block it landed in.

Heading paths are also refreshed in place when the heading set is unchanged.
The stability key covers id/depth/title only, so inserting a block above a
heading used to leave a stale `path` in the cached list, and `onContentClick`
resolves its target with `NodeApi.get(editor, path)`.

perf(editor): stop every block subscribing to global drag state

A long note wraps each top-level block in a Draggable, and four of those
wrappers' hooks read global scalar plugin options, so drag start/end and
marquee start/end re-rendered all N block wrappers.

One subscriber now mirrors isDragging and isSelectionAreaVisible onto the
editable root as data attributes, and the gutter and selection tint read
them through CSS. The dragged-set dimming becomes a boolean selector, which
bails out on Object.is so only the dragged blocks re-render.

perf(editor): mount the block handle menu popover on hover

Opening a long note built a Radix Popover root per top-level block, none of
which the pointer had reached yet. Arm it on the handle's first pointer entry
and release it once the fade-out has run.

The grip keeps its position in the tree so the react-dnd drag connector is
never dropped between pointerenter and mousedown, which is why the popover
anchors to an overlay sibling instead of wrapping the grip.
chore(release): bump version to 0.9.1

feat(import): recognize local PDF metadata in the background

Local PDF imports (picker, drop, library drop) now commit instantly
with filename-derived placeholder metadata: the paper appears in the
tree and library within a second. A new RecognizeMetadata JobCenter
job (cap 2, cancellable, projected into the task bar) then runs the
probe -> recognizer -> identifier-resolution chain and lands the
result via recognize_apply:

- identifier hit: rename the folder to the canonical id through the
  wiki rename transaction (papers/<slug> -> papers/1706.03762),
  including {id}.pdf, catalog path/id rewrite, [[...]] link rewrites
  and rollback; paper:renamed notifies the frontend
- canonical entry already in the library: merge the placeholder into
  it (main PDF or attachments/) and remove the placeholder
- title-only hit: catalog metadata upsert in place
- no match: meta_source=local-unresolved (Edit Metadata to fix)
- user edits made meanwhile (meta_source != local) always win

ParseBody/ParseRefs/layout follow-ups move from commit time into the
runner so they run against the final post-rename path; the frontend
skips its own layout enqueue when recognizePending is set. The
paper:renamed handler suppresses the watcher's external-rename
repair, remaps open tabs/annotations, and refreshes tree + library.

feat(telemetry): report registered agents on app started

Add an anonymous agent summary (sorted template ids + custom agent
count, no names/commands/env) to the `app started` event properties
and `$set` person properties so PostHog can filter and segment users
by installed agents.

fix(plaza): clamp RSS feed card height under WebKit line-clamp bug

WebKit lays out inline-block <button> children with -webkit-line-clamp
using their unclamped scroll height for the parent's line box, leaving
a large empty gap below the clamped summary text. Switching the button
to display:block removes the anonymous line box that caused the leak.

feat(arxiv-daily): probe embedding endpoint before showing cached results

The arxiv daily panel used to render the previous `arxiv_rec_state` from
SQLite on mount and trigger a recompute in the background. When the
embedding endpoint was misconfigured, the recompute would fail with
`recommend.no_embedding` but the stale rows had already been painted, so
the panel looked healthy while the underlying feature was dead.

Add a Host `probe_embedding` liveness check (POST one short input to the
configured `/embeddings` endpoint) and gate the panel on it. The arxiv
daily panel now stays in a "checking" state until the probe passes;
failures flip it into an unreachable state with a Retry / Open Settings
pair, and the recompute path probes first so a dead endpoint never
triggers a wasted ranking run.

The Agent settings pane gets a Test connection button next to the
embedding section header with a status dot (idle / probing / reachable /
unreachable / not-configured) in the same idiom as the Translate and
Layout panes; the dot is the only status indicator — no inline result
line, no toast.

Shared endpoint-resolution helper is hoisted out of `recommend` so
`recommend` and `probe_embedding_endpoint` agree on the same `/embeddings`
URL construction; covered by a unit test.

Co-Authored-By: Qoder <noreply@qoder.com>

feat(feeds): DOM-based Readability scoring for article extraction

Replace string-based tag matching with proper DOM parsing using the
scraper crate. Score candidate containers by class/id hints, paragraph
count, text density, and link density to find the main article content.
Also add a browser-impersonating HTTP client for pages that reject bot
UAs, and always attempt to fetch the original article page regardless
of whether the RSS already ships a summary.

feat(plaza): add category autocomplete for arXiv Daily

Add a popover with cmdk search to the arXiv Daily panel header, letting
users pick from the full arXiv category taxonomy (~150 categories) beyond
the default chips. Selected categories render as removable chips with a
hover-reveal close button. Persist the user's selection in localStorage
so custom categories survive remounts and are not reset by backend
responses.

fix(agent): use native grok CLI instead of npx for Grok Build

Grok Build detected and launched through `npx @xai-official/grok@<pinned>
agent stdio`. Detecting via `npx` made the row report installed on any
machine with Node, which hid the Install button and let the Settings
auto-probe spawn the pinned package — silently downloading the agent
without asking, and timing out against the 15s ACP deadline on a cold
fetch. It also meant Update installed the global CLI that the spawn
command never used.

Detect and launch `grok agent stdio`, and migrate stale registry rows off
the npx launcher so existing installs stop downloading on probe.

fix(feeds): pass JS-challenge 403 with cookie retry when fetching article body

Some sites (e.g. spaces.ac.cn WAF) answer the first visit with 403 +
Set-Cookie + a window.location reload stub. Enable a cookie store on the
browser-impersonating client and replay the request once when the 403
body looks like such a challenge, so the real article is fetched. Also
log a warn instead of silently falling back to the RSS excerpt.

feat(plaza): move source hide/show toggle onto Plaza cards

- Show every source on the Plaza home; hovering a card reveals an eye
  toggle that hides/shows it. Hidden sources stay visible but dimmed so
  they can be restored.
- Drop the source toggle list from the Plaza tree context menu; keep the
  per-source right-click "Hide from sidebar".
- Remove the Plaza description line.

fix(feeds): render LaTeX block environments as display math

KaTeX cannot render MathJax-only environments like equation/multline/
flalign, and remark-math never sees bare \begin{...} blocks from RSS
excerpts. The fetch side now strips unsupported wrappers into $$...$$
while keeping align/gather intact, and the render-side math normalizer
converts raw \begin{env}...\end{env} blocks the same way, stashing
converted regions so bare-command wrapping cannot fragment them.

chore(log): quiet html5ever and network crate debug noise in dev

html5ever logs every parser token and rustls/reqwest log each TLS
frame at Debug, flooding dev output. Cap them at Warn/Info per target.

fix(feeds): unwrap unsupported envs inside cached display math

Older body_markdown caches may hold $$ \begin{equation}… $$ which the
protected-region pass leaves untouched; strip those wrappers in
normalizeMarkdownMath so cached blocks render too.

fix(feeds): clean HTML artifacts in extracted math and fix placeholder restore Blogs embed
line breaks and entities inside raw LaTeX envs; the pre-htmd extraction kept them, so KaTeX choked on '<'. Sanitize math content (br to space, strip tags, decode entities). Also zero-pad the LATEXBLOCK placeholder index: LATEXBLOCK1 prefix-matched LATEXBLOCK10 during restore, repeating one equation across articles with 10+ blocks.

feat(feeds): schema v4 clears stale body_markdown caches

The math conversion changed (env unwrapping, HTML artifact cleanup,
placeholder restore), so cached bodies from older versions may render
broken math. The v4 migration drops body_markdown; items re-resolve on
next open while paper_url is kept.

refactor(feeds): replace article extraction with dom_smoothie

Drop the scraper-based fallback and run fetched article HTML through
dom_smoothie's Readability implementation exclusively.

chore(log): silence html5ever serialize and selectors noise

html5ever's "node with weird namespace" warnings fire on every real-world
blog page; keep only errors. selectors matching traces drop to Warn.

fix(feeds): normalize MathJax macros and blockquote math for KaTeX

Collect \newcommand definitions document-wide and expand them textually
at use sites, sidestepping KaTeX's per-equation scope, builtin-name
collisions (\argmin) and align cell boundaries. Strip \require, degrade
\cancel, resolve \eqref/\ref to display numbers, and unescape older
cached math that htmd markdown-escaped.

Display math is re-fenced onto its own lines only when block-positioned;
mid-sentence $$…$$ (e.g. inside blockquotes) stays single-line so
remark-math inline math matches, and re-fenced lines keep the quote
marker so math stays inside the blockquote.

feat(mcp): add built-in ChatGPT Secure MCP Tunnel supervisor

Spawn and hold a tunnel-client run child from Settings → General → MCP server.
The tunnel gets its own private --profile-dir under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/agentero/mcp-tunnel,
uses CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEY env so the key never crosses argv, and stops on app exit.

so the WebView never sees the plaintext key.

Update backend/mcp, backend/settings, frontend/settings, usage/mcp and

refactor(vault): remove dead catalog storage event branch

The Host watcher ignores all .agentero/ paths, so catalog.sqlite
change events never reach the frontend. Remove the leftover
isCatalogStoragePath short-circuit from use-vault-file-events and

refactor(agent): move remote agent catalog into agent feature

The remote agent catalog is a remote mirror of the agent domain
(reuses CatalogEntry, probe_agent and templates), so it belongs in
the agent feature. Move agent_catalog.rs and its three commands to
agent/remote_catalog(_commands).rs to break the agent<->remote

Also read proxy settings via proxy_settings() instead of

append_title_alias_best_effort is pure frontmatter maintenance and
belongs in the wiki domain. Moving it removes the catalog->wiki

paper_backfill_publication is metadata enrichment over network

Command names stay unchanged for the frontend.

refactor(core): own the headless AppHandle shim

The empty headless AppHandle placeholder lived in features/import
and was borrowed back by lifecycle, refs and zotero, creating three
fake feature-internal cycles. Sink the shim into core::app_handle

refactor(core): replace agent-specific error variants with domain codes

AppError carried AgentNotFound/AgentUnavailable/Acp business
variants, leaking the agent domain into core. Replace them with a

codes and display messages stay byte-identical.

ci(frontend): run dependency-cruiser checks in quality job

build.

refactor(lib): break import cycles and sink vault-file-drag into core

dependency-cruiser reported 22 cycles plus a core-stays-leaf
violation. Resolve them: extract agent catalog types into a pure
api-types leaf (19 cycles shared this one type edge), split window
actions out of shell/ui-store, move layout translate types into
pdf/layout/types, extract inline link styles, and sink the
zero-dependency vault-file-drag module into core. deps:check now
reports zero violations.

refactor(lib): add barrel exports for remaining lib domains

Add index.ts barrels for the twelve lib domains that lacked them
(core, pdf, shell, workspace, markdown, bridge, ui, doctor, mcp,
onboarding, cli, sync) with explicit named re-exports of the
externally consumed surface. Internal implementation files
(workers, mark stores, bridge file-cache) stay unexported. New
code can now import from the domain root; existing deep imports
keep working.

AgentPane grew to 1165 lines in one component. Split it following
the general-pane block pattern: extract useAgentCatalog /
useAgentUninstall / useAgentRegistry hooks and six self-contained
blocks (embedding, user-agent, default agent, catalog rows, custom

transport so RemoteAgentPane reuses it instead of duplicating the
scan/probe/rescan triple. agent-pane.tsx shrinks 1565 -> 336

Follow-up to 976964d2: the isCatalogEntryProbing /
isCustomAgentProbing helpers landed in agent-catalog.tsx but were

refactor(library): split papers library into hooks and row components

PapersLibrary was 1412 lines with sorting, tag filters, column
customization, heatmaps and cell-copy logic inlined. Move pure row
utilities and column metadata into dedicated modules, extract
useLibraryHeatmaps and useCellCopy hooks, and turn the table header
and row renderer into memoized components. The publication refresh
action sinks into lib/paper. papers-library.tsx shrinks to 441

refactor(viewer): sink pdf viewer clusters into hooks and pure modules

PdfViewerInner mixed geometry projection, sidebar panel state,

plus six cluster hooks (pin anchors, active anchors, sidebar

feat(agent): virtualize long chat transcripts

DOM size grew unbounded with conversation length since rows were
all mounted. Render through @tanstack/react-virtual once a session
passes 80 lines, reusing the stick-to-bottom scrollRef so

refactor(import): introduce paper resolver table

Identifier handling was spread across enum matches in parse, mod,
batch and commands (4-6 touch points per new source). Replace
IdentifierKind with a static PaperResolver table (url, doi, arxiv,
isbn, pmid, ads) that owns kind, catalog column, extraction,
translator target and direct fallback per source. The metadata
pipeline keeps Translator-first ordering; skill sources stay on
the dedicated pre-pass. Adding a source now means one resolver

feat(bindings): centralize specta export and generate job types

Move the TypeScript bindings export test out of the translate
feature into app/bindings_test.rs as the single collection point,

commands) and regenerate bindings.ts. The frontend job-center now

fix(bindings): keep generated bindings.ts out of biome formatting

lint-staged ran biome over the regenerated bindings.ts, adding

fix(pdf): let the hovered viewer claim Space for drag panning

Space arming was gated on the keydown target being inside the PDF host (or
exactly body while hovered) and on the panel being dockview's single global
active panel. Reading a PDF normally leaves focus on a tab, the sidebar or the
notes pane, so both gates silently rejected the key and the hand tool never
armed; middle-drag was unaffected because it has no ownership gate.

Claim on hover instead, matching the rule Cmd+F already uses, and fall back to
the active viewer when focus is inside its host or still neutral on body after
a page click. Also widen the native-behavior exclusions to the ARIA roles that
activate on Space (tab/option/checkbox/treeitem and friends) so a focused file
tree row keeps its keypress when the pointer rests over a PDF.

fix(pdf): keep the pan drag alive when WebKit drops pointer capture

The gesture treated lostpointercapture as an end signal. WebKit releases
capture immediately after a pointerdown whose default we prevent, so the drag
ended the instant it began: Space armed the grab cursor and middle-button press
looked live, but no movement ever reached the scroll offsets.

Capture is now best-effort — wrapped so a NotFoundError cannot abort the drag —
and only pointerup/pointercancel end it, with move/up still arriving by
bubbling from the page layers. pan-handler adds a document-level release net so
a button lift outside the viewport cannot leave the drag stuck.

fix(pdf): make Space+left drag equivalent to middle drag

An armed left drag spared buttons and links so they kept their click, while the
middle button panned from anywhere. That made the two entry points to the same
hand tool behave differently: a Space drag starting on a toolbar button or an
in-page citation hit did nothing.

Holding Space already suspends clicks, so once armed the left button is now a
hand tool exactly like the middle one and pans from anywhere but an editable
overlay. With no per-button policy left, the gesture takes a target predicate
again instead of the whole event. The interactive-role list still guards the
bare Space keydown, so a focused button or tree row keeps activating on Space.

feat(pdf): offer sepia and green paper tones

The page colour switch was two-state — light paper or inverted — while
every dedicated reader offers a warm or green tint for long sessions.
Pure white paper at full brightness is what makes marathon reading
uncomfortable, and a low-saturation tint cuts that contrast without
touching the app theme.

The bottom bar toggle becomes a palette popover with four tones: white,
sepia, green and dark. Light tones paint a multiply-blended tint over
the page rasters, so white paper lands exactly on the target colour
while black text stays black and figures keep their saturation — a CSS
filter cannot reach an arbitrary paper colour without desaturating
illustrations. Dark keeps the existing soft invert, since no tint can
brighten text that is already black.

The blend group is isolated on a wrapper around the rasters rather than
on the page shell, so the shell keeps its stacking context and overlays
that overflow the page (comment cards, translate tab, highlight menu)
still paint across page boundaries. The tint sits below the selection,
search and annotation layers, leaving highlight colours untouched, and
Agent crops go through renderPageRect so they are unaffected.
Layout-translate cover blocks follow the active tone instead of always
painting white paper.

The preference keeps its storage key and cross-window event, reading the
legacy "light" value as white so existing installs and already-open
viewers carry over.

fix(deps): clear 32 open Dependabot advisories

is a declared dependency rather than a transitive one.

The nanoid pin is scoped to 3.x because nanoid 5 and 6 are also
installed and fall outside the advisory range.

fix(jobs): settle panicked runners and scope cancellation per job

Runner panics previously skipped finish(), permanently leaking the
per-kind concurrency slot and dedupe key so later jobs of that kind
stayed queued forever. The global CANCELLED set also poisoned task ids
reused after a crash.

run_started now supervises the runner task and settles a JoinError as
Failed (releasing slot/key, emitting job:changed, waking dependents).
Cancellation uses a per-job CancellationToken created on start and
removed on every terminal path, with an RAII bridge to deep
is_cancelled(task_id) pollers; non-JobCenter users keep the legacy
HashSet semantics.

refactor(core): move JobCenter into features and inject telemetry deps

core/jobs violated the invariant that core must not depend on upper
layers: JobKind hardcodes business task kinds, the scheduler calls
features::lifecycle and import orchestration, and its commands use
features::catalog plus integration::remote. Move the module verbatim
to features/jobs (byte-identical apart from paths).

preserving identical values and timing.

refactor(backend): invert remote deps to restore layering

features/ depended upward on integration::remote while integration
reached into feature internals and used tauri command shells as its
internal API, breaking the declared core <- features <- integration
layering in both directions.

- Sink remote handle parsing and proxy env helpers into a pure

- Introduce inversion traits defined in features and implemented in
