fix(jobs): move runner blocking IO onto spawn_blocking

Job runners executed rusqlite queries, file IO and CPU-heavy parsing

* fix(agent): publish a terminal exit status when the last handle drops

The controller's dropped-handle arm returned early when start_kill()
failed, dropping exit_tx without publishing and skipping drain_readers,
so a waiter saw "terminal exit watcher dropped" instead of a real status
and the output readers were detached rather than drained. A failed kill
means the process is already gone, which is exactly when child.wait()
has a status to report.

running must kill it and publish a status. That arm had no coverage.

simplified_agent_cwd was applied on the run and warm paths only, so
session/list and session/load still handed agents the canonicalized

AcpTerminalManager::with_cwd was wired into the run path only, so an
agent creating a terminal during warm-up or session load ran commands in

fix(paper): report one merged progress for concurrent asset downloads

PDF and TeX source download concurrently under a single task id, but the
frontend still weighted them as sequential phases (PDF 0-50%, TeX
50-100%). Whichever stream finished first mapped to 100%, and the
Math.max latch in updateBackgroundTask held the bar there while the
other stream kept fetching -- so the row read "100%" above a detail line
that was still counting up.

Move the aggregation to the Host, the only side that knows how many
streams actually run: AssetProgressAggregator merges their byte counters
into one job:progress event, with the slot count fixed up front as the
denominator. The frontend now only clamps. A stream still running with
no Content-Length keeps the merged total unknown instead of letting the
other one read 100%, and each PDF candidate URL restarts its own byte
count.

This also fixes the mirror case: a PDF-only import has no TeX stream, so
it could never pass 50% until the job terminated.

fix(agent): actionable Antigravity sign-in and stale-session prompt recovery

ACP error JSON ("Authentication required ... authMethods ..."), even when
the agy CLI itself reported signed in (the adapter probes `agy models`,
which needs network reachability). And prompts could fail with agy's
internal "File not found" when its conversation brain files went missing
(e.g. after an agy upgrade), leaving the session unusable.

- Host tags auth-required run failures with `AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED agent=<id>`;
  chat/mobile/PDF-ask/plaza surfaces map it to i18n copy instead of raw JSON.
- Chat failure toast gains a "Sign in" action: new `agent_login_terminal`
  command opens the system terminal at `<command> <args> --login`
  (Enter-to-confirm UX); the agy login TUI closes itself once signed in,
  then the user retries the prompt.
- Prompt failures containing "File not found" retry once with a fresh
  session on the same ACP connection (buffers cleared), recovering
  sessions whose server-side state vanished.

fix(agent): harden auth-required handling for heterogeneous machines

The reporting machine differs from dev machines (portable node on another
drive, custom PATH, possibly older agy-acp). Close the gaps that only
show up there:

- Mark command-level invoke rejections with AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED too (the
  send hook's catch path surfaces the invoke error directly, bypassing
  the agent:failed event); emit_run_failed stays idempotent.
- Parse the marker unanchored so prefixed (`acp: ...`) strings map to the
  i18n sign-in copy as well; chat send catch paths now route through
  displayAgentError.
- agent_login_terminal resolves the command against the merged agent env
  (login-shell PATH) before composing the terminal line, so the login
  command works even when a fresh terminal's PATH lacks the npm shim dir.

Translation, embedding and OCR body parsing each require users to supply

Add a Host-side module resolving a built-in "agentero" provider from

buildable without secrets: a build with no injected key reports the

The key never crosses IPC. builtin_provider_status returns only

feat(translate): route the built-in provider through Hunyuan-MT

The built-in "agentero" provider talks to a dedicated MT model
(tencent/Hunyuan-MT-7B), not an instruct model. Such a model only follows
the template it was tuned on, so reusing the OpenAI-compatible rule block
would buy nothing and risk the rules being echoed into the output. It gets
its own source: the literal single-line template sent as one user message
with no system message, and no source-language slot (the template has no
place for one; the model auto-detects).

The [[n]] batch protocol depends on instruction-following, which this model
does not do, so markers must never reach it. The Host splits a batched
payload on line-start [[n]] markers (ascending from 1; a mid-line or
out-of-order marker ends the scan so prose is never cut), translates each
segment as its own request with bounded in-order concurrency (buffered(3),
so results need no index plumbing), and rejoins byte-identically to the
frontend's buildNumberedPayload. Empty segments are dropped: fewer segments
than expected makes parseNumberedTranslation return null and fall back to
per-paragraph translation instead of mis-aligning paragraphs. Masked ⟦n⟧
inline placeholders pass through untouched.

The id stays out of FREE_PROVIDERS (the CLI gates --provider on that list
and then calls with no key, so it would accept a provider it cannot
authenticate) and out of COMMERCIAL_PROVIDERS (that list drives the WebView
credential cards, which the built-in must not render).

Credentials resolve in the Host command before the await-free BYOK path:
the built-in branch overwrites key/base URL/model from the compile-time
module and returns the translate.no_builtin_key marker when this build
carries no key, instead of falling through to an unauthenticable request.

feat(settings): resolve built-in embedding and OCR credentials

Choosing the built-in provider must not require any user-supplied
credential, so both consumers resolve it in the Host:

- EmbeddingSettings gains `source` ("builtin" | "custom"). It is plain
  #[serde(default)], not a default fn returning "builtin": a legacy
  settings.json with a populated BYOK endpoint but no `source` key would
  otherwise be indistinguishable from an explicit built-in choice.
  normalize() infers it instead — explicit value wins, any populated BYOK
  field (an all-`*` mask counts) implies custom, all-empty implies builtin.
  embedding_config() returns the gateway triple unless the source is
  custom, and falls through to the stored values when this build carries no
  key so `recommend.no_embedding` still fires.
- The layout credential getters special-case the built-in id, which has no
  providerConfigs card. Resolving there rather than per caller keeps every
  consumer correct; prompt/language/force-OCR stay unset because the VLM
  engine derives its prompt from the model id and the other two are
  MinerU-only. `agentero` is registered as a parser backend reusing that
  engine, now carrying its own id so a fallback note reads
  "agentero failed: …".

Two things make the choice stick, and both are easy to miss: PARSER_BACKENDS
gains the id (normalize runs on every save and persists the reset, so an
unlisted backend could never be selected), and default_translate_provider /
default_parser_backend prefer it when a key was compiled in — read_file
returns AppSettings::default() when settings.json is missing, so the Rust
defaults, not the TS ones, decide a fresh install.

LAYOUT_BACKENDS is deliberately untouched and default_layout_backend stays
"local" unconditionally: layout analysis runs on the bundled offline
PP-DocLayoutV3 ONNX model, and moving it to the gateway would bill every PDF
for no gain. A test guards that, plus the key containment (the provider-config
whitelist drops any built-in card, so the compiled-in key can never reach
settings.json) and the engine registration (an unknown backend degrades to
the local parser silently rather than erroring).

Regenerates bindings for the new `source` field and the parserBackend doc.

fix(build): forward built-in provider env vars to rustc

could ship a stale or empty key with no signal at all.

variables, which also enables the gitignored repo-root .env fallback for
the built-in provider. Verified: injecting a key now recompiles the host
crate, and omitting it leaves the binary clean.

probe_embedding accepted a webview-supplied baseUrl override and resolved

fix(settings): make built-in availability gating reliable

The embedding source select offered "Agentero built-in" unconditionally, so
an unkeyed build showed a selected source with no fields, no status dot and
no test button — nothing to indicate it was inert. Gate the item on
availability, keeping it listed but disabled when it is the stored value, as
the translate and layout panes already do.

A failed status query cached null, and the cache short-circuits on
"resolved", so one transient IPC error hid the provider until the window
reloaded. Only cache successes; concurrent callers still share one request.

Onboarding read availability from render state, which starts false and
settles asynchronously, so clicking "use system default" before the query
returned still wrote the static frontend default — the exact clobber the
previous fix targeted. Await the authoritative status at click time instead,
which also removes the need for a settled flag on the hook.

fix(windows): stop doctor probes from opening console windows

Opening Settings -> Diagnostics pops up black console windows titled with the
agent executable path. The pane probes on mount, and every probe went through
`diagnostic_command`, which spawned `cmd` / `powershell` / `<tool> --version`
without `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. The release binary is a GUI subsystem app, so
Windows allocates a visible console for each console child - one window per
probed tool, and per registered Agent (a Hermes catalog entry plus a custom
Hermes profile produce two identical hermes.exe windows).

- Split `diagnostic_command` into `base_command` + `hide_console_window` so the
  host runtime and Agent probes share one place that sets CREATE_NO_WINDOW,
  matching lifecycle / version_check / mcp tunnel.
- Add a Windows regression test pinning the cmd / PowerShell / exe routing the
  wrapper sits on (`creation_flags` has no std getter).
- Document the platform constraint in docs/backend/doctor.md.

fix(windows): stop startup device probe from flashing a console window

Launching Agentero pops a black console window before the UI paints. The
`app started` telemetry payload collects `device_model`, which on Windows
shells out to `reg query HKLM\HARDWARE\DESCRIPTION\System\BIOS`, and that
child was spawned without `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. The release binary is a GUI
subsystem app, so Windows allocates a visible console for it.

Process tracing shows the installed 0.9.7 build behaves the same way: `reg`
starts shortly after the webview, and `conhost` follows within ~40ms. It is
just easier to miss there because the flash lands while the window is still
blank. So this is not caused by running the unpackaged binary.

- Extract `device_model_command` and set `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, matching
  lifecycle / version_check / mcp tunnel / doctor.
- Add a Windows regression test pinning the registry query the wrapper sits
  on (`creation_flags` has no std getter).
- Note the platform constraint in docs/backend/telemetry.md.

fix(editor): keep note content after prose `<` comparisons (Fix #533)

remarkMdx hard-crashes on a `<` followed by anything that cannot start a
JSX name (digits, `-`, `.`, CJK punctuation), e.g. the `<0.5B` comparison
in the report. Plate's recovery then cuts the document at that `<` and
silently drops every block after the first line of the remainder.

Escape such stray `<` as `<` in prepareMarkdownForDeserialize — the
single choke point for all deserialize entry points (open, external
reload, paste, embeds, export). Neither the MDX tokenizer nor Plate's
htmlToJsx can mistake an entity for a tag, and remark decodes it back to
a literal `<` in the editor. Code fences, block math and inline
code/math spans are skipped, already-escaped `\<` is left alone, and
tags/fragments/comments are untouched.

feat(host): add agentero-web generic page proxy with host allowlist

Web papers (html_url, no local PDF) stream in a sandboxed iframe, so the
page must come from us for its selections to reach the app. Register an
`agentero-web` custom scheme (features/web/proxy.rs) that rebuilds
text/html responses: strips upstream CSP / X-Frame-Options, injects
`<base href>` so relative subresources load from the real origin without
widening the proxy's SSRF surface, and injects WEB_BRIDGE — the
postMessage selection/scroll/shortcut/external bridge the viewer chrome
consumes.

Unlike the per-site discovery proxies this one serves arbitrary hosts,
so it is gated by a process-level allowlist (allowlist.rs): public DNS
names only (no IP literals / intranet names), every redirect hop
re-checked, credential headers never forwarded. `web_proxy_allow_host`
lets the viewer ensure a host before pointing the frame at the proxy.

fix(plaza): let the ModelScope panel pan horizontally (#557)

* fix(plaza): let the ModelScope panel pan horizontally

The panel clamped the site's 1280px paper pages to its own width to stop
them clipping at the left edge (#550), which also left no horizontal
overflow — nothing to pan. Keep the site's desktop layout instead and let
the frame's document be the horizontal scrollport; clamping the pages would
leave no room to pan at all.

Two things then need handling, both because a frame is not a browser window:

- The site centres a page action with `scrollIntoView({ block: "center",
  inline: "center" })`, and in a frame narrower than its layout that drags
  the whole document sideways, hiding the left edge (#550 again). The bridge
  wraps `scrollIntoView` and restores the horizontal offset of every scroll
  container the call moved; vertical scrolling is untouched.
- Wheel deltas are not reliably delivered to, or chained by, the panel, so
  the bridge pans the document itself: it remembers the position at the
  start of the frame and, only if the document did not move horizontally by
  the next frame, adds the accumulated deltaX (Shift+wheel included). The
  event is never cancelled, so a diagonal gesture keeps scrolling vertically
  and an in-page horizontal scroller keeps priority.

The site's layout root is scrollable in script too and was being parked 10px
right, clipping the card gutter; its smooth scrolling is disabled and it is
pinned to 0.

fix(pdf): preview trackpad pinch zoom and commit it once (#556)

Trackpad pinch and Cmd+wheel zoomed in EmbedPDF's fixed steps: every
step was 10% below 100% and 20% between 100% and 200%, so a slow pinch
appeared not to respond at all while a fast one jumped, and every step
re-laid out the scroller and re-rasterized the visible pages.

The gesture now drives a CSS transform preview that keeps the point
under the fingers fixed, and the real zoom is committed once when the
gesture ends.

- wheel-zoom: gestures report one cumulative magnification per gesture
  instead of wheel-equivalent deltas for a fixed-step coalescer (deleted
  along with it); the passive/non-passive wheel switching and the WebKit
  gesturestart/change/end path are kept
- zoom: clampZoomPreviewScale holds the preview inside 50-300%,
  zoomPreviewTranslate anchors it on the gesture point
- wheel-zoom-handler: the commit lands in a single paint. The layout
  effect that runs with the new scroller layout writes the scroll the
  zoom plugin derived for that focus and drops the transform, so the DOM
  never paints the new layout scaled a second time by the preview -- a
  compositing stall over a document-height element. That scroll is not
  recomputed from geometry on purpose: the plugin centers content
  horizontally once it is narrower than the viewport, so a hand-rolled
  anchor lands half a page off when zooming in from a small zoom.
- will-change: transform for the duration of the gesture, so the pages
  rasterize once and the compositor scales that raster

Committing once also stops the zoom from superseding the viewport's own
deferred scroll request, which is what walked the viewport to the start
of the document on a fast pinch.

fix(viewer): register reloaded pdf buffers under a fresh document id

The app-wide PDFium engine caches documents by documentId. A reloaded
buffer kept the stable tab id, so the new bytes were rejected: EmbedPDF's
registry destroy closes the old document only after the replacement open
is queued (destroy is async; the worker queue ranks openDocumentBuffer
above closeDocument), and PdfCache.setDocument re-uses the existing
context for a known id while freeing the freshly loaded pointer. The pane
therefore kept rendering the stale PDFium document until a full unmount.

Fold a per-ArrayBuffer revision into the id so each re-read from disk
registers a fresh document; URL sources keep the base id.

users as unrecoverable: the CLI install toast told them to run
`npm config set cache` by hand, which often did not help. Managed
lifecycle runs now probe the effective npm cache for writability and
inject `npm_config_cache` pointing at an Agentero-owned directory when
the system cache cannot be written, so installs succeed without user
action. A healthy cache is left untouched so the warm download cache is
preserved.

Also routes the About panel's CLI/Finder install toasts through
`lifecycleErrorMessage` (same pattern as the agent pane), fixes the zcode
Windows install command to use the platform-aware template constant
(the hardcoded string left the import unused, breaking Windows clippy),
and decodes PowerShell `-EncodedCommand` payloads in the kimi test so it
passes on Windows.

fix(mcp): kill tunnel-client on stop and sweep orphans at startup

watch_exit held the child mutex across wait(), so stop()'s try_lock
never won and start_kill never ran; kill_on_drop was lost because the
global async runtime is never dropped at process exit. Every app exit
and every Stop click therefore leaked a tunnel-client process.

Poll the child with short lock holds so stop() can win the mutex, and
fall back to an OS kill by pid when it cannot. At startup, sweep any
tunnel-client pointing at our private profile dir - single-instance
makes every such match an orphan of a previous run.

fix(agent): close the EPERM gaps in managed npm installs

The earlier cache-isolation fix (1c03213b) probed only the npm cache root,
which passes when the root is user-writable but a root-owned `_cacache`
child is not. macOS `sudo` keeps `$HOME`, so a single `sudo npm` run leaves
`_cacache/tmp`, `index-v5` and `content-v2` owned by root inside the user's
own `~/.npm`; the probe then skips the override and npm fails mid-install
with the intermittent EPERM users report "sometimes". Probe the subtree npm
actually writes into, not just the root.

Codex was also the last adapter still installed into the global npm prefix
on Unix, which is commonly root-owned, so `npm i -g` fails there without
sudo. Route install, uninstall, remote install_command and the manual
instructions through CODEX_ACP_INSTALL_COMMAND, mirroring the claude/pi/
zcode/dsh user-prefix pattern.

refactor(core): converge duplicated paper helpers across crates

The same small helpers had grown several near-identical copies — six

`normalize_alias`, `safe_relative_path` and `normalize_id` — so a fix to
one copy could silently skip the rest. Each now has a single home
(`features/paper/util.rs`, `wiki/frontmatter.rs`, `fs/path.rs`,
`scholar_api/mod.rs`) and the former call sites import it.

`normalize_title` existed three times with three different transforms.
They are renamed to `title_similarity_key`, `title_compact_key` and
`title_match_key`, each documented so the wrong one cannot be picked by
name.

`looks_like_path`, `parse_tag_spec` and a new `lookup_paper_ref` (path/id
resolution with an explicit `Ambiguous` outcome) move into the paper
catalog: CLI and MCP had byte-identical copies and now share one
resolver while keeping their own messages and CLI exit-code semantics.
`split_off_frontmatter` had already drifted between the Zotero codec and
the MCP notes tools; it now lives in `features/markdown/frontmatter.rs`
with tests pinning BOM, CRLF, non-fence `---` and unterminated blocks.

refactor(core): use normalize_rel_separators for inline path normalization

Twenty sites hand-rolled the same normalisation — `replace('\\', "/")`
followed by `trim_matches('/')`, some chained across lines or split into
two statements — instead of calling the helper that already documents
those exact semantics. They now call `normalize_rel_separators`, and the
two single-call-site `norm_rel` wrappers that only forwarded to it are
gone.

Sites with a different operation order (`trim_matches` before `replace`,
or no `replace` at all) are intentionally untouched: they diverge for
leading/trailing backslashes, so folding them in would change behaviour
and belongs in a separate decision.

the label-key mapping, the card header, the `label + input` field row

fix(i18n): stop rendering raw keys, placeholders and stale copy

Three places put something other than the intended text in front of the
user.

`jobPanelDetail` passed only `current`/`total` to
`refreshMetadataTaskDetail`, whose text also interpolates `{{updated}}`,
`{{failed}}` and `{{empty}}` — a metadata-refresh job that had not been
picked up yet rendered those placeholders literally in the background
tasks panel. That queued window is the only case this fallback covers
(the executor reports real counts as soon as it starts), so zeroes are
the truthful values there.

The `clearUsage` failure branch fell back to
`general.privacy.clearUsage.done`, i.e. an error toast reading "Activity
history cleared". It now reports the thrown error, matching the other
call sites in the pane.

`theme-step` used the action key `theme.uiThemeSelect` ("Select {{name}}")
as the default theme's name, which hardcoded the English "Default" and
double-wrapped the aria-label into "Select Select Default". It reuses
`settings:appearance.uiTheme.default` — the same string the
settings-appearance pane shows — and declares the `settings` namespace so
the cross-namespace key type-checks.

fix(plaza): localize feed error fallbacks instead of leaking raw codes

`callApi` falls back to its `fallback` string when a Host error carries no
message, and the plaza modules wrote those fallbacks as i18n-key-shaped
codes ("feeds.listFailed", "recommend.probe_failed"), expecting
`hostErrorKey()` to translate them. The table only held the eleven
content-level codes, so the nine operation codes missed the lookup and the
raw code was toasted verbatim.

The operation codes now map to a new `plaza.feeds.errors.opFailed` entry
in both locales. Unknown codes still return `null`, so host-supplied
messages keep flowing through untouched.

The arXiv recommendation view had the same leak without a table to fix:
when the probe failed with the `ERR_PROBE_FAILED` sentinel, the code was
both rendered as the empty-state sub-line and toasted, even though that
empty state already carries localized copy and a retry button. The
sentinel is now recognised and skipped; genuine host errors still surface.

`recommend.failed` (the `recommendArxiv` fallback) has no sentinel yet and
can still reach `handleError`'s toast — left alone, since fixing it needs
a call on the copy or a new empty-state branch.

fix(agent): fall back to legacy session models field for hermes

hermes-agent still advertises its model catalog via the pre-stabilization
top-level `models` field on session/new instead of the standard
configOptions (category=model) selector; its migration upstream
(NousResearch/hermes-agent#81067) is not yet merged. The official ACP
Rust schema drops that field on deserialize, so warm returned no models
and the composer picker showed the empty state.

Send session/new as an UntypedMessage to keep the raw JSON, parse the
typed NewSessionResponse from it as before, and when configOptions yield

prefixes (e.g. opencode-zen:*) map to picker groups, and a current model
absent from the catalog is injected so it stays selectable.

(Claude/Codex/Dsh/OpenCode) are unaffected.

fix(agent): give warm session/new a 30s budget for heavy agents

Warm's session/new used the shared 15s ACP timeout, but heavy BYOA agents
(Hermes profiles) build the full agent — provider inventory, tools, MCP — on

when the agent is healthy. This made hermes-research's warm time out after 15s
and surface an empty model picker, while the lighter catalog-hermes succeeded.

initialize already got a 30s budget for the same reason; give warm's
session/new the matching ACP_NEW_SESSION_TIMEOUT. Interactive turns keep the
responsive 15s budget.

fix(pdf): reapply page rotation in normalized engine mode

The scroll/selection/tiling patches assumed normalizeRotation: true makes
PDFium report display sizes with /Rotate baked in. The engine does the
opposite: page.size stays in unrotated content space and page.rotation
keeps the metadata; layout, tiles and raster must re-apply it. Stripping
page.rotation rendered /Rotate 90 pages portrait with sideways tables,
and pdfPageRenderRotation gated page.rotation on normalizedRotation so
the base raster always rendered at rotation 0.

Drop the plugin-scroll and plugin-selection patches to restore the
upstream effectiveRotation formula, keep the tiling patch to its dpr
typing and tile-placeholder scope, and make the base raster always add
page.rotation. Engine semantics are pinned by a dedicated test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(pdf): pin normalizeRotation engine contract

Documents with /Rotate report unrotated content-space sizes plus
rotation metadata under normalizeRotation: true, and the display space
only appears when the caller passes that rotation to the renderer. A
generated /Rotate 90 fixture pins both modes so the viewer wiring is
not "fixed" backwards again.

fix(pdf): rotate tiling raster and placement for /Rotate pages

The tiling plugin computed tile rects in unrotated content space and
rendered them without rotation, so /Rotate 90 pages painted sideways
portrait tiles over the fixed landscape base layer, overflowing the
page shell and overlapping the next page. Extend the plugin-tiling
patch: pass effective rotation to the engine in renderTile, include
rotation in tile ids, and transform each tile screenRect into the
rotated container via transformRect before CSS placement. Verified in
an isolated-port harness: page 4 tiles raster landscape-upright with
no overflow and no visual overlap.
